Lessons.Title: Ways to Find Angle Measurements (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will the purpose of this optional lesson is for you to use the attributes of figures (symmetry, equal side lengths, right angles) to reason about angle measurements.
Previously, you analyzed the attributes of two-dimensional figures and used them to find side lengths and perimeters. In this lesson, you use the attributes of figures to find unknown angle measurements and to practice drawing line-symmetric shapes. Both activities in the lesson deepen your understanding of line symmetry.

2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up: How Many Do You See: Symmetry in a Star (10 minutes); Activity 1: Before and After, Angle Edition (25 minutes); Activity 2: Angular Fish (15 minutes); Cool-down: Stage Symmetry, Revisited (5 minutes)
Source-goal geometric reasoning: Use symmetry, equal sides and right angles to deduce missing angles; reflected corresponding angles have equal measurements.

Edulytics worked explanation: Mark the given reflection line and known angle measurements. Equate the corresponding angles that symmetry preserves. If a 70° angle is bisected by a reflection line, each half is 35°. Use right and straight angle totals to check any remaining angle.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (not gated original): A symmetry line divides an 84° angle into two equal angles. Find each one.
Original student diagrams, teacher card sorting, paper folding, and physical drawings require figure-by-figure / teacher validation.
